title: Analyzing Chris Bumstead's training program
summary: NH analyses Chris Bumstead's published 5-day body-part split day by day. He praises the compound choices and openers but criticises excessive exercise counts, junk volume, sandbagged sets, poor day pairing, no supersets and badly placed rest days, concluding that naturals could cut about 45% of it. He also mocks the supplement promotion around it.
claims: Pro bodybuilders look the way they do because of drugs, but training still separates competitive pros from others
CBum's split is named like a bro split but closer to a gentleman split in spirit because it doesn't stick to the day labels
A 5-on/2-off split should build fatigue to peak on Friday to justify two rest days
Opening back day with deadlifts (4 sets, 12/10/8 to failure) is good; heavy compounds aren't bad for hypertrophy
Bent-over rows after deadlifts double up on lower back fatigue; rotate deadlifts and bent-over rows week to week instead
A Mr Olympia needing assisted pull-ups would reflect a poor size-to-strength ratio
Drop straight-arm pulldowns and keep one row; a second and third row variation becomes junk volume naturals can't recover from
Body-part splits push you to smash the same muscles past recovery just to justify the session
Natural back day suggestion: deadlifts alternating weekly with bent-over rows, weighted pull-ups, rows, then superset small muscles
Three chest exercises is enough per session; cable flies and push-ups after that is too much
Fixed 15-rep biceps work chases the pump; biceps also need intensity to grow
Writing deadlifts as 10/8/8 then to failure suggests sandbagging early sets; bad practice
Biceps don't pair well with chest; pair chest with shoulders and triceps, and back with lower body
Naturals could cut about 45% of his chest and biceps day and get similar results
Hamstrings and glutes pair well on the same day
Start hamstring day with a hip hinge, not leg curls, then use curls for the stretch
4x15-20 is too high for straight-leg deadlifts; 4x6-10 is better since cardio limits high reps
The program has almost no supersets because body-part splits make them impossible; mixing muscle groups saves time
Shoulders and triceps is the most synergistic pairing for a body-part split
Start shoulder day with a press rather than lateral raises
Front raises are fine if pain-free
11 exercises for shoulders and triceps would take naturals three hours for almost no gain
Triceps kickbacks are at the bottom of programming importance
Efficient session: horizontal press, vertical press, maybe chin-ups, lateral raises supersetted with face pulls
A quad-only day makes little sense; never open leg day with leg extensions
Only 2x8 squats followed by 4x40 leg press puts the volume in the wrong place; past ~20 reps it's junk
Better leg day: squat, hip hinge, maybe leg extensions, go home
His heaviest days are Monday and Tuesday, so the weekend rest is misplaced
Most YouTube viewers aren't on drugs, yet copy pro bro splits and see no progress: too much volume and no focus on intensity
His reported 7000 kcal diet matters more for an enhanced pro than for naturals
BCAAs, omega-3s and pre-workout are not why CBum looks the way he does; affiliate supplement lists exploit viewers
exercises: rotate with deadlifts week to week
overlaps lower back fatigue with deadlifts
vertical pull after a floor pull
better placed on an upper day
fine back-off press if used well
needs intensity, not just pump reps
hamstring hip hinge; high reps cardio-limited
